children: Global brokerage Macquarie has initiated coverage on NSE with an outperform rating and a target price of ₹1,965, ahead of the exchange’s listing on the market today. The brokerage views NSE as “The Dominator”, citing its leading market share and power, while highlighting its full set of services, technology stack and deep liquidity.
Macquarie said entrenched network effects, industry-leading profitability and cash underpin its positive outlook on NSE. It described the exchange as the lynchpin of India’s financialisation.

According to Macquarie, platform expansion will drive revenues, although there could be near-term pressure from the Closing Auction Session (CAS). The brokerage said the long-term industry outlook remains constructive.
Macquarie said NSE’s superior fundamentals justify a premium multiple and sees room for further re-rating if new products accelerate.

Macquarie described BSE as a “challenger” and a credible competitor to NSE, pointing to its pivot to index options. The brokerage said BSE’s platform expansion and share gains create revenue and margin optionality, supporting strong cash generation.

The brokerage said BSE’s earnings growth, margin expansion and platform optionality underpin its positive outlook. It also said BSE is riding India’s financialisation wave, with structural tailwinds for margins and platform expansion expected to drive revenue.

Despite potential near-term strain from the Closing Auction Session, Macquarie’s long-term forecast for the industry remains constructive. The brokerage said there is room for further re-rating of BSE.
Macquarie said the market is yet to fully reflect BSE’s potential for share gains in cash equities and F&O, growth in non-transaction businesses and significant cash generation.
SEBI regulations prevent NSE from trading on NSE itself. Therefore, NSE will list and trade on BSE.

Jefferies estimates this will add 1-2 per cent to BSE’s FY27E earnings. Assuming NSE’s own daily turnover trades at levels similar to HDFC Bank, the brokerage estimates ₹70 crore in combined cash and stock-option revenue for BSE.

title: Macquarie initiates coverage on NSE with ‘Outperform’, sets ₹1,965 target price
